newsitem.title: FRANCE: Brazil boosts Airbus airshow sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil boosts Airbus airshow sales.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie said Wednesday that Brazilian airline TAM agreed to buy up to 10 of its A330-200 widebody twin-engined jets in a deal valued at around $1 billion.
Airbus made the announcement at the Paris air show, making it the first big prestige order of the week in the event's traditional marketing battle between industry giants Airbus and Boeing Co.

Airbus senor vice president for sales John Leahy told a news conference it was the first order for the A330-200 in Latin America. TAM is to buy five A330-200s and take options for another five in a deal valued at more than $1 billion, based on list prices of $106 million to $115 million a plane.

TAM's president and chairman Rolim Adolfo Amaro said at the joint news conference that his Sao Paolo-based regional airline would use the aircraft to expand into international routes, first to the United States and then to Europe from 1998.
Amaro also said that United Technologies unit Pratt & Whitney was to get the engine order in preference to a rival bid from British firm Rolls-Royce Plc .
P&W senior vice president Craig Muhlhauser said the work could be worth up to $250 million including spare parts and support, based on a quoted price for the PW4000 series engines of $8 million.
